definitions.explanation: The melodic or rhythmic quality of music, speech, or poetry.
A technical term in music theory referring to the system of dividing the octave into intervals (e.g., equal temperament, just intonation).

examples.japanese: {美|うつく}しい{音律|おんりつ}が{響|ひび}く。
この{詩|し}には{独特|どくとく}の{音律|おんりつ}がある。
examples.english: This poem has a distinctive rhythm.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{俳句|はいく}は{五七五|ごしちご}の{音律|おんりつ}で{構成|こうせい}されている。
examples.english: Japanese haiku are composed in a 5-7-5 rhythm.

examples.japanese: ピアノの{音律|おんりつ}を{調整|ちょうせい}する。
examples.english: To adjust the tuning of a piano.

examples.japanese: バロック{音楽|おんがく}と{現代|げんだい}の{音楽|おんがく}では{音律|おんりつ}が{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: Baroque music and modern music use different tuning systems.

examples.japanese: {平均律|へいきんりつ}は{最|もっと}も{一般的|いっぱんてき}な{音律|おんりつ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Equal temperament is one of the most common tuning systems.

notes:
FORMATION:
{音|おん} (sound) + {律|りつ} (rule, rhythm).

USAGE:
Sense 1 is used broadly for the musical or rhythmic quality of any sound, including poetry and speech. Sense 2 is a technical music theory term referring to specific tuning systems like {平均律|へいきんりつ} (equal temperament) or {純正律|じゅんせいりつ} (just intonation).

RELATED:
- {旋律|せんりつ}: melody (a specific melodic line)
- リズム: rhythm (the loanword, more casual)
- {調律|ちょうりつ}: tuning (the act of tuning an instrument)
